quote.text: The spectacle is not a collection of images; it is a social relation between people that is mediated by images.
quote.author: Guy Debord, The Society of the Spectacle (1967)

stories.headline: The Cardboard Economy
stories.dek: Nobody plans to spend seven thousand dollars on a picture of a lizard. It starts with a pack — and two tribes who would never share a lunch table end up buying from the same auction house.

stories.headline: What Changed at the Gate
stories.dek: A new balance floor on your miles, more Scoot metal to the north — and the one nonstop that makes this weekend's Grand Tour a three-hour hop.

stories.headline: The Girls on the Mound
stories.dek: Taiwan turned baseball into a concert — and then started importing Korea's idols to headline it. For twenty years Asia bought Korean cool. This is the first market to manufacture a version good enough to sell back.

stories.headline: The Outbreak the World Walked Away From
stories.dek: A rarer Ebola strain, no licensed vaccine, and a war on top of it — the fastest-spreading epidemic on record is unfolding in the near-absence of the donor that used to run point.

stories.kicker: Singapore · The Week Before the Rally
stories.headline: A Quiet Sunday, and the One Next Week
stories.dek: Before the set-piece, a week to ask what "Go Beyond" will actually mean for the grocery bill, the flat and the childcare fees — when the Prime Minister stands up seven days from now.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Buy It Once — No. 1 · Sleepwear
stories.headline: Read the Momme, Ignore the Adjective
stories.dek: A new desk, and the reader's own question to open it: if you wanted one luxury set of pyjamas, what do people actually lust over? The answer starts at the cloth — and a 28°C bedroom rewrites the order.

stories.headline: The Chips Are Frozen. The Weights Walk Free.
stories.dek: Washington spent a year building a licence regime to meter advanced silicon into China. The thing that actually matters to a home lab crossed the border anyway — as a download.

stories.kicker: The Kit · The Object You Queue For
stories.headline: A Pocket Camera With a Twelve-Month Order Book
stories.dek: No pre-order theatre, no wearable gimmick — the Ricoh GR IV is the anti-hype carry, a magnesium snap-shooter so in demand you grow into the wait.

stories.headline: A Venetian Legend Gets New Keys
stories.dek: The Danieli — a Gothic palazzo on the lagoon since the fourteenth century — reopens under Four Seasons, its pink-marble atrium and gilded staircase intact, its nightly rate pointedly unpublished.

stories.kicker: Screen & Sound · The Record for the Room
stories.headline: Jungle Make the Sundown Album Again
stories.dek: The British funk-soul collective's fifth, "Sunshine," is a no-skips groove record engineered for good speakers — and a small argument about the cost of a winning formula.

stories.headline: It Was Never the Hours
stories.dek: The 2026 evidence quietly retired the stopwatch. The damage screens do runs mostly through two things they push out — movement and sleep — and those are the two a parent can actually guard.

stories.headline: Goldilocks, With an Oil Tail
stories.dek: A record within reach on Wall Street, gold at a fresh high, and a long bond that refuses to fall — three things that should not all be true at once, reconciled by a barrel.

stories.headline: Two Thirty-Second Tests, Read for Decades
stories.dek: The longevity crowd obsesses over aerobic fitness. A 2026 cohort makes the quiet case for the other axis — raw strength — and hands you two free home benchmarks to track it.

stories.kicker: The Diary · The Season Fills Up
stories.headline: What to Book Between Now and the New Year
